content.title: Patient education and self-care (Table 12)
content.summary: Patient education is vital to improve self-care, quality of life (QOL), reduce readmissions and mortality. Education should be tailored to the individual, based on evidence or expert opinion, and reinforce messages regularly. Lack of knowledge and misunderstandings contribute to insufficient self-care.
general_educational_approaches: Provide information in a variety of formats that take into account educational grade and health literacy; consider approaches with active roles for patients and caregivers (e.g., ask-tell-ask, teach-back, motivational interviewing).
Recognize barriers to communication (language, social skills, cognition, anxiety/depression, hearing or visual challenges).
Recommend resources such as HFmatters.org; offer help and guidance to use them and discuss arising questions.
Invite patients to be accompanied by a family member or friend.
content.reference_notes: Key topics to include are recommended in Table 12.

table_12.title: Patient education and self-care
columns: Goal for the patient and caregiver

rows.Goal for the patient and caregiver: To understand the cause of their HF, symptoms and treatment choice.

Goal for the patient and caregiver: To understand prognosis and the different possible phases in the HF trajectory.
To make joint treatment decisions that recognise the patient's position on the HF trajectory.
rows.Professional behaviour and educational t: Sensitively communicate information on prognosis at time of diagnosis, during decision making about treatment options, when there is a change in the clinical condition and whenever the patient requests.

Goal for the patient and caregiver: To be able to make joint decisions about medication.
To understand the indications, benefits, and the need for long-term adherence.
Professional behaviour and educational t: Provide written and oral information on indication, benefits, dosing, effects and side effects.
Discuss practical issues such as optimal time-schedule and what to do in case of a missed dose.
